newsitem.title: USA: Nashua attributes Q2 loss to lower sales.
newsitem.headline: Nashua attributes Q2 loss to lower sales.

text.p: Nashua Corp Thursday attributed its $1.9 million loss, or $0.30 a share, in the second quarter to lower sales in key areas, such as dry toner, cartridges and paper for laser printers.

"Our financial performance continues to be disappointing and well below our expectations primarily due to lower volume in major product areas," said the company's chief executive, Gerald Garbacz, in a statement.
Nashua said the $1.9 million quarterly loss included a $3 million charge, or $0.24 a share, for restructuring distribution channnels and cutting its workforce.
The maker of specialty imaging products is restructuring its commercial products division, which makes specialty papers, and copier and printer supplies.

"During the quarter, we recognized restructuring and unusual charges of $3 million principally targeted at improving the competitiveness and profitability of the commercial products segment," Garbacz said. "We anticipate the annualized benefit of these actions, once fully implemented, will be over $5 million."

Nashau said its commercial products group posted a $2 million operating loss in the second quarter, compared with a $100,000 loss in the same period the year before. Quarterly sales dropped to $43.2 million from $51.8 million the year before.
Nashua said the unit's sales decline mainly reflected lower demand for dry toner, laser printer cartridges, and copier paper.

By contrast, sales of company's photo group increased to $37.3 million from $36.3 milion in the second quarter of 1996. The company ascribed the increase to higher pricing in the United States, offset by lower unit volumes and a favorable foreign currency effect.

Overall, Nasha sales dropped to $80.5 million from $103.6 million. Its loss from continuing operations was $1.9 million, or $0.30 a share, compared with a operating profit of $18.7 million, or $2.91 a share.
Looking forward, Gorbacz said he expected sales to pick up amid stronger demand. He added he expected three new toner and laser products to generate about $10 million in annual sales.
"We believe the second half of 1997 will be marked by improvement in the financial performance of all of our major operating units," he said.
